title: Most Adults Cannot Pass This Teacher's Entrance Exam
summary: Explore Understanding Learners, Assessment and Safety, Goals and Numbers, Access and Evidence, The Final Lesson across five six-question rounds.

landing.intro:
Think like a thoughtful teacher.
Put learning at the centre.

about.body:
Five rounds offer different angles on this challenge: Understanding Learners, Assessment and Safety, Goals and Numbers, Access and Evidence, The Final Lesson. Each round contains six distinct questions.

Choose one of four answers and move on automatically. There is no time limit. A short rewarded ad opens the quiz, each next round and the final result. The target is 24 correct answers out of 30. The result describes this quiz attempt only.

For entertainment and general learning only. This is not an accredited teacher-training, admission or employment exam. Safeguarding procedures and professional requirements vary by location; follow the rules that apply where you work.

steps: Press Start, watch a short rewarded ad and begin.
Choose one answer per question and progress through five rounds.
Complete all 30 questions to reveal your result. You can then unlock the full breakdown.

insights.overview: Your classroom score at a glance

teacher-q1.question: Which approach gives a teacher the clearest quick picture of whether the whole class understood a new idea?

answers.a1: A brief check in which every learner responds

teacher-q2.question: A learner gives an incorrect answer. Which response is most likely to support learning?

answers.a1: Move immediately to someone else
answers.a2: Ask them to explain their thinking, then guide them with focused questions
answers.a3: Announce the correct answer and continue

teacher-round1-new1.question: What does modelling a task give learners?

answers.a1: An example of the process they are being asked to use

teacher-round1-new2.question: Why ask learners to explain an answer?

answers.a1: To understand their reasoning
answers.a4: To assume every correct answer reflects understanding

teacher-round1-new3.question: What is constructive feedback most useful for?

answers.a1: Identifying a specific next step
Recalling information from memory

teacher-q3.question: What is the usual name for assessment used during learning to help adjust teaching?

answers.a1: Final assessment

teacher-q4.question: A learner discloses information suggesting they may be at risk of harm. What is the best general response?

answers.a1: Promise complete secrecy
answers.a3: Wait to see whether they mention it again
answers.a4: Listen calmly, avoid promising secrecy and follow the appropriate safeguarding procedure

teacher-round2-new1.question: What is summative assessment mainly used for?

answers.a1: Judging achievement at a point after learning
A set of criteria used to describe or assess performance

teacher-round2-new3.question: Why should a teacher avoid investigating a safeguarding disclosure beyond their role?

answers.a1: Specialist procedures protect the learner and the response
answers.a4: The teacher should promise secrecy instead

teacher-round2-new4.question: What should a safeguarding note distinguish?

answers.a1: The learner's words from the adult's interpretations
answers.a4: Only information that confirms an assumption

teacher-q5.question: Which learning objective asks learners to make the most complex judgment?

answers.a1: Compare two explanations and support a conclusion with evidence
answers.a3: List the days of the week

teacher-q6.question: A class has 30 learners working in equal groups of 5. How many groups are needed?

teacher-round3-new1.question: A learner answers 18 of 24 questions correctly. What percentage is that?

teacher-round3-new2.question: A lesson lasts 45 minutes. Three equal activities fill the lesson. How long is each?

answers.a1: 15 minutes

teacher-round3-new3.question: Which objective is easiest to assess directly?

answers.a1: Compare two sources and cite one supporting detail from each

teacher-round3-new4.question: What does scaffolding mean in learning?

answers.a1: Temporary support that can be reduced as competence grows
answers.a2: Permanently doing every task for learners
answers.a4: Using only one method for everyone

teacher-q7.question: What does differentiated instruction most accurately involve?

answers.a1: Giving every learner completely different subject content
answers.a2: Lowering expectations for the entire class
answers.a3: Adapting access, support or challenge while keeping meaningful learning goals
answers.a4: Allowing only confident learners to answer

teacher-q8.question: When is an assessment described as reliable?

answers.a1: When it contains the greatest number of questions
answers.a2: When every learner receives a high mark
answers.a3: When it can be completed quickly
answers.a4: When it produces reasonably consistent results under similar conditions

teacher-round4-new1.question: What is an accessible instruction likely to include?

answers.a1: Clear language and an appropriate format
Whether it measures the intended knowledge or skill
answers.a3: Whether it takes the longest time
answers.a4: Whether learners all get identical marks

teacher-round4-new3.question: Why use more than one source of evidence about learning?

answers.a1: One task may not show the whole picture
answers.a3: All evidence must produce the same score

teacher-round4-new4.question: What does a reasonable learning adaptation preserve?

answers.a1: A meaningful opportunity to work toward the learning goal
answers.a3: An identical route for every learner

teacher-q9.question: Which instruction is most likely to help learners begin a new task successfully?

answers.a1: Give a short sequence, model an example and check understanding
answers.a2: Explain every possible exception before stating the task
answers.a3: Write one vague sentence and begin immediately
answers.a4: Ask learners to guess the success criteria

answers.a1: Revising a draft after feedback
answers.a2: Presenting another person's words or ideas as your own without acknowledgement

answers.a1: Add evidence that supports your second claim

teacher-round5-new2.question: A source is paraphrased in a report. What is still normally needed?

answers.a1: Acknowledgement of the source
answers.a2: A claim that the idea is original
answers.a3: No reference because the wording changed

teacher-round5-new3.question: What is a useful response when many learners share the same misconception?

answers.a1: Revisit the idea using evidence and a different explanation
Using evidence to consider what worked and what to change
answers.a2: Assuming the first plan was perfect
